parsedVerdict.reasoning: AdvanceOrderUseCase.execute does the usual application-layer orchestration. It loads the aggregate through the repository port, hands the state transition to the domain (order.advanceTo with the injected clock's time), coordinates a side effect across services (stock dispatch on shipment), saves through the port, and maps the result to a DTO. It contains no persistence, transport or framework code. Every collaborator is a domain port or an application helper. The one conditional, `if (target === 'shipped')`, is a borderline case. It could be read as a domain rule ("shipping dispatches stock"). But it coordinates two separate domain collaborators (the Order aggregate and StockReservationService), and use cases commonly own that kind of cross-service coordination. The transition rules themselves stay in Order.advanceTo. No ADR prose contradicts this. I judge the file to match its application role.
